title: How to Tell If Your Thermostat Is Reading Wrong
h1: How Can You Tell If Your Thermostat Is Reading the Wrong Temperature?
description: Compare your thermostat to a separate thermometer to see if it reads wrong. Learn the common causes, simple fixes and when a thermostat needs a technician.
quick_answer: Put a reliable thermometer next to the thermostat for about 15 minutes, away from your hands and any vents, and compare the readings. If they're more than a couple of degrees apart, the thermostat is likely off. Other clues are a system that runs too long or too short, rooms that feel different from the setting, and frequent cycling.
body:
A thermostat that reads a few degrees off can make the whole house uncomfortable. It can also make your AC or furnace run longer than it needs to. Often the cause is simple, like where the thermostat is mounted or a pair of tired batteries.

How do I test my thermostat's accuracy?

You don't need special tools. Here's an easy check:

  1. Get a reliable digital or bulb thermometer.
  2. Tape it to the wall right next to the thermostat, at the same height.
  3. Wait at least 15 minutes without touching either one.
  4. Compare the readings.
  5. Repeat at a different time of day, like a sunny afternoon and an evening.

A difference of one degree is normal. If they're consistently two or more degrees apart, the thermostat may need adjustment, relocation or replacement.

What signs suggest the thermostat is off?

  • The house feels warmer or cooler than the number on the screen.
  • The system turns on and off every few minutes.
  • The system runs for long stretches and the house overshoots the setting.
  • The temperature reading jumps around.
  • The screen is dim, blank or flickering.
  • The system doesn't respond when you change the setting.

Why does a thermostat read the wrong temperature?

Most of the time, the thermostat is fine but its location isn't. A thermostat only knows the temperature of the spot where it hangs. Common problem spots include:

  • Direct sunlight from a window or skylight in the afternoon
  • Near a supply vent, which blows hot or cold air right onto it
  • On an exterior wall that heats up on summer afternoons
  • Near the kitchen, a lamp, a TV or other heat sources
  • In a hallway that doesn't match the temperature of the main living spaces
  • Above a drafty hole in the wall where wires come through

That last one is common. Air from the attic or wall cavity can blow through the wire hole behind the thermostat. In inland homes, hot attic air in summer can fool the sensor. Sealing that hole often fixes the reading.

What can I fix myself?

Try these simple steps:

  1. Replace the batteries if your thermostat uses them.
  2. Clean it. Dust inside the cover can affect the sensor. Remove the cover and gently blow out dust.
  3. Block the sun. Close blinds or move lamps and electronics away.
  4. Use the offset setting. Many digital and smart thermostats have a temperature offset or calibration setting in the menu. Your manual will explain how to adjust it.
  5. Check that it's level. Older mechanical thermostats with a mercury switch need to be level to read correctly.

Older mercury thermostats contain a small amount of mercury. If you replace one, don't throw it in the trash. Take it to a household hazardous waste drop-off.

When should I call a technician?

Call if the reading is still off after these steps, if the thermostat needs to move to a better wall, or if you're upgrading to a smart thermostat that needs a common wire. Wiring changes, new wire runs and system compatibility are best handled by a technician, especially with heat pumps and multi-stage systems.

Sometimes the thermostat isn't the problem at all. A dirty filter, low refrigerant, leaky ducts or a struggling system can all make the house feel off even when the thermostat is accurate. A technician can check both.

Our HVAC technicians install, relocate and set up thermostats, including smart and zoned systems. If your home has uneven temperatures, we can also look at whether zoning would help.

Where is the best place for a thermostat?

An interior wall in a main living area, about five feet off the floor, out of direct sun and away from vents, doors, windows and appliances. If your home has hot and cold areas, a smart thermostat with remote room sensors can average temperatures from several rooms.

Also give the thermostat clear space. Bookshelves, picture frames and furniture placed tight around it can trap heat and change what it reads.
faqs: Can a thermostat be off by a few degrees?
Yes. Location, sunlight, drafts through the wire hole, dust and aging sensors can all throw it off. A difference of one degree is normal. Two or more is worth looking into.
How do I recalibrate a digital thermostat?
Many digital and smart thermostats have a temperature offset setting in the installer or advanced menu. Your manual will show how to find it. Older models may not have one.
Why does my thermostat say 72 but it feels warmer?
The thermostat may be in a cooler spot than the rest of the house, or humidity may be making it feel warmer. It's also possible the system isn't keeping up because of a dirty filter or duct problems.
Is it worth upgrading to a smart thermostat?
For many homes, yes. Smart thermostats offer scheduling, remote control and remote sensors that help with uneven rooms. Make sure the model is compatible with your system before buying.
